introduction: The `af` binary (`cmd/af`) and its command shell (`internal/toolio`) give every agent-fox command one contract: a single JSON envelope on stdout with a fixed status and exit-code table, `needs_human` with a `--context` resume, a forge client that cannot write under `--dry-run`, a fetchable `--schema`, uniform resolution of the positional `<issue|file|text|->` input, and a git-ignored run directory under the checkout holding the envelope, the event stream and the ledger. In this scope the binary answers only `--version`, `--schema` and `help`; work commands land in later specs on this shell.

glossary.DryRunForge: `toolio.DryRunForge(inner)`: an issuex.Client decorator that passes reads through and refuses every write with an error wrapping `toolio.ErrDryRun`, recording it as a planned side effect.
glossary.command path: The one or more words a command is registered under ("triage", "gate run"); it is the envelope's `tool` value.
glossary.envelope: The single JSON object (`toolio.Envelope`, schema_version "5.0.0") that every af command invocation other than --version, --schema and help writes to stdout, with a fixed field set and order.
glossary.failure: `*toolio.Failure{Category, Message, Retryable, FixHint}`: the error type a command returns to set the envelope's `error` object and category.
glossary.ledger: `<run_dir>/ledger.jsonl`: append-only JSON lines `{seq, ts, kind, data}` that later commands use to record what they measured.
glossary.outcome: `toolio.Outcome{Status, Summary, Result, NeedsHuman}`: what a command returns when it did not fail; status is done, unverified or needs_human.
glossary.resume: `needs_human.resume {argv, flag}`: the argv to re-run, with argv[0] "af", plus the flag ("--context") to append with the human's answer.
glossary.run directory: `<dir>/.agent-fox/run/<id>/`, the per-invocation local state holding envelope.json, events.jsonl, ledger.jsonl and optionally report.md and panic.txt; git-ignored by `<dir>/.agent-fox/.gitignore`.
glossary.run id: The run directory's name, `YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS_<6 lowercase hex>` in UTC.
glossary.shell: `toolio.App`: the dispatcher that parses flags, resolves input, builds the forge client and run directory, calls the command's Run and turns its outcome or error into the envelope.
glossary.test command: A command registered only inside `internal/toolio` tests to exercise each shell behaviour without a real work command.

requirements.title: Binary, command dispatch, help and version
requirements.rationale: One binary with one dispatch rule lets every later command inherit the same invocation grammar.

criteria.condition: the leading non-flag arguments of an invocation match one or more registered command paths
criteria.action: dispatch to the command with the longest matching registered path and pass it the remaining arguments
criteria.contract: the envelope's `tool` equals the dispatched command path (e.g. "gate run" over "gate")

criteria.condition: `af` is invoked with no arguments or with a first word that matches no registered command path
criteria.action: print a `usage` envelope whose `tool` is "af" and whose `error.message` lists every registered command path
criteria.contract: exit code 2; status `usage`; error.category `usage`

criteria.action: parse each command's own flag.FlagSet with ContinueOnError, accepting flags before or after the positional argument and treating `--` as the end of flag parsing, so that `af X ./bug.md --dir repo` and `af X --dir repo ./bug.md` yield the same parsed flags and positional

criteria.condition: flag parsing fails, or more positional arguments are given than the command declares (one by default)
criteria.action: discard the flag package's own output and print a `usage` envelope naming the offending flag or argument
criteria.contract: exit code 2; status `usage`; nothing written to stderr

criteria.condition: `-h`, `--help`, `af help` or `af help <command>` is invoked
criteria.action: print plain-text help on stdout: the registered command list, or the named command's synopsis and flags
criteria.contract: exit code 0; stdout is the help text and is not JSON

criteria.condition: `af --version` is invoked
criteria.action: print `{"name":"af","version","commit","build_time","go_version"}` taking the values from the `-ldflags -X` variables of package main, else from runtime/debug.ReadBuildInfo (main module version, vcs.revision, vcs.time), else version "dev" with empty commit and build_time
criteria.contract: exit code 0; stdout is exactly one JSON document

criteria.condition: `make build` is run
criteria.action: build every package and write `bin/af` from `./cmd/af` with `-ldflags` setting main.version, main.commit and main.buildTime from the Makefile's VERSION, COMMIT and BUILD_TIME; `cmd/af` holds only package main wiring that exits with the code `App.Main(ctx, args, stdin, stdout, stderr)` returns
criteria.contract: `bin/af --version` reports the Makefile's VERSION; `go build ./cmd/af` succeeds

criteria.condition: `--schema`, `--version` or `--help` appears anywhere on a command line
criteria.action: answer that request without resolving input, building a forge client or creating a run directory
criteria.contract: exit code 0; no forge request is made and no `.agent-fox` directory is created

requirements.title: The envelope
requirements.rationale: A consumer must never have to tell a missing field from an empty one, so the shape is fixed and always complete.

criteria.action: write exactly one JSON object to stdout for every command invocation other than --version, --schema and help, indented by two spaces and followed by one newline, and write nothing else to stdout
criteria.contract: stdout parses as a single JSON object

criteria.action: emit the envelope fields in the order schema_version ("5.0.0"), tool, run_id, status, exit_code, summary, input, result, needs_human, error, warnings, artifacts, side_effects, next, usage, started_at, finished_at, duration_ms, with every field present, arrays as `[]` never null, and `fix_hint` either null or an object with only the keys flag, env, var and suggest
criteria.contract: JSON key order equals the listed order for every status

criteria.action: for any envelope, set `needs_human` non-null if and only if status is `needs_human`, set `error` non-null if and only if status is `failed` or `usage`, and set `exit_code` to the code the status maps to and the process returns
criteria.contract: status/exit_code pairs are exactly done/0, failed/1, usage/2, needs_human/3, unverified/4, and App.Main returns exit_code

criteria.action: write started_at and finished_at as RFC 3339 UTC timestamps with millisecond precision, duration_ms as the invocation's wall time in integer milliseconds, and, when no brain ran, usage as `{brain: "", cost_usd: 0, cost_source: "none", input_tokens: 0, output_tokens: 0, turns: 0}`

criteria.condition: the invocation has a run directory or was given `--output <path>` (accepted by every command)
criteria.action: write the same envelope to `<run_dir>/envelope.json` and to the `--output` path before printing it to stdout
criteria.contract: each file's content is byte-identical to the stdout envelope

criteria.condition: `<run_dir>/envelope.json` or the `--output` path cannot be written
criteria.action: add the warning `envelope_unwritable` (run directory copy) or `output_unwritable` (--output copy) to the stdout envelope and leave its status unchanged
criteria.contract: stdout envelope carries the warning; exit code is the status's code

criteria.condition: writing the envelope to stdout fails
criteria.action: return the exit code of the envelope's status from App.Main regardless of the write error
criteria.contract: App.Main returns the status's exit code

requirements.title: Status, failures and warnings
requirements.rationale: Every way a command can end, including a crash, maps to one status and one exit code so callers can branch without parsing prose.

criteria.condition: a command returns an Outcome with status done, unverified or needs_human and a nil error
criteria.action: copy the outcome's status, summary and result into the envelope
criteria.contract: exit code 0 for done, 4 for unverified, 3 for needs_human

criteria.condition: a command returns an error that is a `*toolio.Failure`
criteria.action: set `error` to `{category, message, retryable, fix_hint}` from the Failure, with status `usage` when the category is `usage` and status `failed` for any other category
criteria.contract: exit code 2 for category usage, 1 otherwise

criteria.condition: a command returns a non-nil error that is not a `*toolio.Failure`
criteria.action: report status `failed` with error.category `internal` and the error's text as error.message
criteria.contract: exit code 1; error.retryable false

criteria.condition: a command panics
criteria.action: recover the panic, write the stack to stderr and, when a run directory exists, to `<run_dir>/panic.txt`, and print one envelope with status `failed` and category `internal`
criteria.contract: exit code 1; stdout holds exactly one envelope

criteria.action: for any envelope, keep `summary` to a single line containing no newline character, and fill it with a one-line description whenever the shell sets the status itself (usage, internal, cancelled, timeout)
criteria.contract: envelope summary contains no newline or carriage-return character

criteria.action: for any sequence of warnings raised through Run.Warn or by the shell, list each distinct (code, message) pair once in the order first raised and leave the status unchanged
criteria.contract: a done run with warnings still has status done and exit code 0

criteria.action: define the failure categories usage, auth, forge, io, cancelled, timeout and internal as exported constants of internal/toolio
criteria.contract: toolio exports a constant for each of the seven category strings; error.category of a shell-set failure is one of them

criteria.action: raise only warning codes that match `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`

requirements.title: Cancellation and timeouts
requirements.rationale: A stopped or overdue command must still leave a parseable envelope and a bounded exit time.

criteria.condition: the process receives SIGINT or SIGTERM while a command runs
criteria.action: cancel the command's context, and report status `failed` with category `cancelled` when the command then returns an error
criteria.contract: exit code 1; error.category `cancelled`

criteria.condition: the command's context was cancelled by SIGINT or SIGTERM
criteria.guard: the command has not returned within 10 seconds
criteria.action: stop waiting for the command and print an envelope with status `failed` and category `cancelled`
criteria.contract: exit code 1 within 10 seconds of the signal plus envelope write time

criteria.condition: a command opts into `--timeout <duration>`
criteria.action: run the command under a context deadline of the given duration, using the command's declared default when the flag is absent and no deadline when the value is 0

criteria.condition: the `--timeout` deadline expires before the command returns
criteria.action: report status `failed` with category `timeout`, retryable false and fix_hint `{flag: "--timeout", suggest: <twice the given duration>}`
criteria.contract: exit code 1; error.fix_hint.flag "--timeout"

criteria.condition: the `--timeout` value does not parse as a Go duration or is negative
criteria.action: refuse the invocation before calling the command
criteria.contract: exit code 2; status `usage`

requirements.title: needs_human and --context
requirements.rationale: A command that stops on a question must tell the caller exactly how to resume with the answer, without the shell holding state between runs.

criteria.condition: a command returns an Outcome with status needs_human and a non-empty question
criteria.action: set `needs_human` to `{question, options, resume}` with options as `[{id, label}]` whose ids are "A", "B", … in order, and an empty options array meaning free text is expected
criteria.contract: exit code 3; status `needs_human`

criteria.action: set `needs_human.resume` to `{argv, flag: "--context"}` where argv is the invocation as received with argv[0] replaced by "af" and any `--context` values already present retained
criteria.contract: running resume.argv with `--context <answer>` appended re-invokes the same command with all prior answers plus the new one

criteria.condition: a command opts into `--context <text>`
criteria.action: accept the flag repeatedly and pass the values to the command verbatim, in command-line order, as Run.Context, attaching no other meaning to them
criteria.contract: Run.Context equals the given values in order

criteria.condition: a `--context` value is empty
criteria.action: refuse the invocation before calling the command
criteria.contract: exit code 2; status `usage`

criteria.condition: a command returns status needs_human with an empty question, returns a question with any other status, or returns more than 26 options
criteria.action: treat the outcome as a command bug and report status `failed` with category `internal`
criteria.contract: exit code 1; needs_human null

requirements.title: Positional input classification
requirements.rationale: Every command that takes `<issue|file|text|->` must read it the same way so callers learn one rule.

criteria.condition: a command that declares an input receives the positional argument `-`
criteria.action: read stdin until EOF as the input body
criteria.contract: input.kind "stdin", input.origin ""

criteria.condition: the positional argument is accepted by issuex.ParseIssueURL
criteria.action: read the thread with the run's forge client via ReadIssue, set Input.Issue and Input.Thread, and set IsPullRequest when either the URL or thread.Issue.IsPR says so
criteria.contract: input.kind "issue", input.origin equals the IssueRef.URL()

criteria.condition: the positional argument starts with `http://` or `https://` but is not accepted by issuex.ParseIssueURL
criteria.action: refuse it with a message naming the accepted GitHub and GitLab issue and pull/merge-request URL forms and a fix_hint naming GITHUB_API_URL and GITLAB_API_URL for self-hosted forges
criteria.contract: exit code 2; status `usage`; no forge request

criteria.condition: the positional argument names an existing regular file relative to the process's working directory
criteria.action: read the file as the input body
criteria.contract: input.kind "file", input.origin is the file's absolute path

criteria.condition: the named file has a NUL byte in its first 8 KiB, the argument names a directory, or the file exists but cannot be read
criteria.action: refuse the input: "not a text file" for the NUL case, a directory error for a directory, an io failure for an unreadable file
criteria.contract: NUL or directory: exit code 2, status `usage`; unreadable: exit code 1, status `failed`, category `io`

criteria.condition: the positional argument matches none of the stdin, issue URL, http(s) or file rules
criteria.action: use the argument with surrounding whitespace trimmed as the input body
criteria.contract: input.kind "text", input.origin ""

criteria.condition: a command that requires an input gets no positional argument, or the resolved input body is empty after trimming whitespace
criteria.action: refuse the invocation before calling the command
criteria.contract: exit code 2; status `usage`

criteria.action: set the envelope's `input` to `{kind, origin, truncated}` from the resolved Input, and to `{kind: "none", origin: "", truncated: false}` when the command declares no input or none was resolved

requirements.title: Issue rendering, truncation and read errors
requirements.rationale: The rendered body is what a brief shows a model, so its format, its size bound and its failure categories are fixed.

criteria.action:
render an issue thread as the heading `<GitHub|GitLab|Forge> <issue|pull request> <ref> (state: <state>)` (GitLab when the host contains `gitlab`, GitHub when it contains `github` or is empty, Forge otherwise), then `Title:`, `Author:` and `Labels:` lines with the labels line omitted when there are none, then the trimmed body, then each comment as `
--- comment by <login> ---
<body>
`, then `
[... further comments not read ...]
` when the thread is truncated
criteria.contract: Input.Body for an issue equals RenderThread(ref, thread) before truncation

criteria.condition: the input body exceeds 131072 bytes
criteria.action: cut the body at the last UTF-8 boundary at or below 131072 bytes, append `\n[... input truncated at 131072 bytes ...]\n`, set truncated, and raise the warning `input_truncated`
criteria.contract: input.truncated true; warnings contain code `input_truncated`

criteria.action: for any valid UTF-8 input body, produce a Body that is valid UTF-8, is at most 131072 bytes plus the marker's length, and equals the original when the original is at most 131072 bytes

criteria.condition: the issue thread read from the forge has Truncated set
criteria.action: set input.truncated and raise the warning `input_truncated`
criteria.contract: input.truncated true

criteria.condition: the issue thread read from the forge has CommentsErr set
criteria.action: raise the warning `comments_unreadable` and continue with the issue body
criteria.contract: warnings contain code `comments_unreadable`; status unaffected

criteria.condition: ReadIssue returns a not-found error while the forge client is unauthenticated
criteria.action: report a failure saying the issue may be private, with fix_hint `{env: "GITLAB_TOKEN"}` for a GitLab host and `{env: "GITHUB_TOKEN"}` otherwise
criteria.contract: exit code 1; status `failed`; category `auth`

criteria.condition: ReadIssue returns a not-found error while the forge client is authenticated
criteria.action: report a forge failure
criteria.contract: exit code 1; status `failed`; category `forge`; retryable false

criteria.condition: ReadIssue returns a rate-limit error or a transport error
criteria.action: report a retryable forge failure
criteria.contract: exit code 1; status `failed`; category `forge`; retryable true

requirements.title: Forge client construction and --dry-run
requirements.rationale: The forge is the one effect the shell hands out itself, so the shell guarantees a dry run cannot write to it.

criteria.condition: a command declares that it uses a forge
criteria.action: build the client through App.NewForge (default issuex.NewWithOptions) with UserAgent "af/<version>" and Dir set to --dir, using Options{Repo: ref.Repo} for an issue URL input, else Options{Repo: <parsed --repo>} when the command opts into --repo and it is given, else Options{}, and set Run.Target to the resolved repository; build no client for a command that does not declare one
criteria.contract: Run.Forge is non-nil exactly for commands that declare forge use

criteria.condition: `--repo` is rejected by issuex.ParseRepo, or `--repo` and an issue URL input name different repositories
criteria.action: refuse the invocation before calling the command
criteria.contract: exit code 2; status `usage`

criteria.condition: client construction fails with ErrAmbiguousForge or ErrUnsupportedForge and the input is an issue URL
criteria.action: report a usage failure carrying issuex's message and fix_hint `{env: "GITHUB_API_URL"}`
criteria.contract: exit code 2; status `usage`

criteria.condition: client construction fails with ErrAmbiguousForge or ErrUnsupportedForge and the input is not an issue URL
criteria.action: hand the command issuex.NewNoOp() and an invalid Run.Target and call the command
criteria.contract: the command runs; Run.Target.Valid() is false

criteria.condition: a command that was given a forge client returns or panics
criteria.action: close the client exactly once before writing the envelope
criteria.contract: the client's Close is called once

criteria.condition: a command opts into `--dry-run` and the flag is given
criteria.action: set Run.DryRun true and hand the command toolio.DryRunForge(inner) instead of the inner client
criteria.contract: Run.DryRun true; Run.Forge is the decorator

criteria.action: pass Authenticated, Close, GetRepository, ReadIssue, ListIssues, ListComments, ReadPullRequest, ReadChangedFiles, GetPRState, GetCIChecks and GetPRReviews through to the inner client, and implement MaxBodyLength returning issuex.MaxBodyLength(inner)
criteria.contract: issuex.MaxBodyLength(DryRunForge(gitlabClient)) is 1048576

criteria.action: for any call to CreateIssue, UpdateIssue, CloseIssue, AddComment, AddLabels, RemoveLabel, CreateLabel, CreatePullRequest, PostReviewComment, MergePullRequest or ClosePullRequest, send no request, return an error wrapping toolio.ErrDryRun, and append the side effect `{kind: <method in snake_case>, target: <IssueRef.String() or Repo.String()>, state: "planned"}`
criteria.contract: an httptest forge records zero write requests; errors.Is(err, toolio.ErrDryRun); envelope side_effects lists each refused write as planned

requirements.title: Run directory, events and ledger
requirements.rationale: Local, ignored state per run lets later submit and land commands resume work and audit what happened without touching the repository's own files.

criteria.condition: a command declares a run directory
criteria.action: create `<dir>/.agent-fox/run/<id>/` before calling Run, with <dir> the absolute --dir (default `.`) and <id> `YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS_<6 lowercase hex>` from UTC time and random bytes, also under --dry-run; set the envelope's run_id and add the artifact `{kind: "run_dir", path}`, and when the command calls RunDir.WriteReport write `report.md` and add the artifact `{kind: "report", path}`
criteria.contract: run_id matches `^[0-9]{8}_[0-9]{6}_[0-9a-f]{6}$`; artifact paths are absolute; run_id is null for commands without a run directory

criteria.condition: --dir does not exist or is not a directory
criteria.action: refuse the invocation before creating anything or calling the command
criteria.contract: exit code 2; status `usage`

criteria.condition: the drawn run directory already exists
criteria.action: draw a new random suffix, up to 5 attempts in total, and fail when all collide
criteria.contract: after 5 collisions: exit code 1; status `failed`; category `io`

criteria.action: create `<dir>/.agent-fox/.gitignore` with content `*\n` only when it is missing, opening it with O_EXCL so that a concurrent run neither fails nor overwrites it, and never edit the repository's own `.gitignore`
criteria.contract: `git status --porcelain` shows nothing under .agent-fox; the repository .gitignore is byte-identical before and after

criteria.condition: toolio.OpenRunDir(dir, id) is called
criteria.action: return the existing run directory when id matches the run id format and the run exists, and otherwise return a usage failure without touching the filesystem outside .agent-fox/run
criteria.contract: ids such as `../x` or a missing run give a *Failure with category `usage`

criteria.action: for any sequence of RunDir.Record(kind, data) calls, append lines `{seq, ts, kind, data}` to `<run_dir>/ledger.jsonl` with seq 1..n, and return them in the same order with the same kinds and data from RunDir.Ledger(); the shell itself records nothing in the ledger

write events as JSON lines `{seq, ts, run_id, type, data}` with seq starting at 1 and each line flushed when written, to `<run_dir>/events.jsonl` and appended to `--emit-events <path>` (accepted by every command), emitting `run_start` `{tool, argv, input_kind}` first, one `warning` event per warning, the command's own events from Run.Emit, and `run_end` `{status, exit_code, duration_ms}` last
criteria.contract: events.jsonl's first type is run_start and last is run_end; seq is strictly increasing by 1

criteria.condition: an event cannot be written to the run directory or the --emit-events path
criteria.action: raise the warning `events_unwritable` once and continue the run
criteria.contract: warnings contain exactly one `events_unwritable`; status unchanged

requirements.title: Schema, golden files and documentation
requirements.rationale: Consumers validate the envelope against a fetchable schema, and the docs are the contract's human-readable copy.

criteria.condition: `af --schema` is invoked
criteria.action: print the JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) embedded from `internal/toolio/schema/envelope.schema.json`, with schema_version `const: "5.0.0"`, `required` listing every envelope field in envelope order, `result` open, and each registered command's result schema under `$defs` keyed by its path with spaces replaced by `_`
criteria.contract: exit code 0; stdout is one JSON document

criteria.condition: `af <command> --schema` is invoked
criteria.action: print the envelope schema narrowed to that command: `tool` is `const` the command path and `result` is null or the command's declared result schema
criteria.contract: exit code 0; stdout is one JSON document

criteria.action: compare the schema output with the committed golden files `internal/toolio/testdata/schema.golden.json` (no commands registered) and `cmd/af/testdata/schema.golden.json` (the real binary's registrations), failing on any difference and rewriting them when run with `go test ./... -update`
criteria.contract: `go test ./...` fails when either golden file differs from the output

criteria.action: fail when the schema's `required` list differs, in names or in order, from the JSON tags of toolio.Envelope's fields
criteria.contract: `go test ./internal/toolio` fails on drift

criteria.action: ship `docs/cli.md` (af and its global flags, the envelope field by field, the status and exit-code table, error categories and warning codes, needs_human and --context, --dry-run, --schema, --version and help, the run directory layout), `docs/configuration.md` (GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN, GITLAB_TOKEN, GITHUB_API_URL, GITLAB_API_URL and the .agent-fox directory) and `docs/model-usage.md` (af runs no model and reads no vendor key in this release); update `README.md` with cmd/af/, internal/toolio/ and bin/af and `docs/architecture.md` with the run directory layout and ledger formats, removing the claim that docs/cli.md already existed; and commit the output of `make doc`
criteria.contract: the three new files exist and name every status, exit code, category and warning code the shell defines

criteria.action: pass `make check` (gofmt, go vet and go test) with no network access, using only httptest servers on loopback for forge tests
criteria.contract: `make check` exits 0 offline

execution_paths.title: A tool fetches the version and the envelope schema from the real binary

steps.action: runs `af --version` and then `af --schema` against the binary built by `make build`
calls toolio.App.Main with the ldflags version, commit and build time and exits with its code
detects the --version / --schema request before any input, forge or run-directory work
prints the version JSON document, then the embedded schema with every registered command under $defs
receives two JSON documents, each with exit code 0, the schema matching cmd/af/testdata/schema.golden.json

execution_paths.title: A dry run reads a GitHub issue and is refused every forge write

steps.action: runs the test command with a GitHub issue URL pointing at an httptest forge, `--dry-run` and `--dir <tmp checkout>`
creates `<tmp>/.agent-fox/.gitignore` and `<tmp>/.agent-fox/run/<id>/`, builds the forge client from the URL's host and wraps it in DryRunForge
reads the issue thread via ReadIssue and renders it with RenderThread into Input.Body
calls AddComment and CreatePullRequest on Run.Forge, receives errors wrapping ErrDryRun, and returns done
records the GET for the issue and comments and zero write requests
writes envelope.json and events.jsonl (run_start … run_end) into the run directory and prints the envelope with status done, input.kind issue and two planned side effects

execution_paths.title: A command stops on a question and is resumed with --context

steps.action: runs the test command with a text input
returns status needs_human with a question and two options
prints an envelope with exit code 3, options A and B, and resume {argv: ["af", …], flag: "--context"}
re-runs resume.argv with `--context B` appended
receives Run.Context ["B"] and returns done
prints an envelope with status done and exit code 0

execution_paths.title: An unknown command yields a usage envelope

steps.action: runs `af nosuch`
finds no registered path matching `nosuch`
prints a usage envelope with tool "af" and an error message listing the registered commands
observes exit code 2 and nothing on stderr

execution_paths.title: An unauthenticated read of a private GitLab merge request fails with an auth hint

steps.action: runs the test command with a GitLab merge-request URL pointing at an httptest forge and no GITLAB_TOKEN
builds an unauthenticated GitLab client from the URL's host
answers the merge-request read with 404
maps the unauthenticated not-found error to an auth failure
prints an envelope with status failed, category auth, a message saying the issue may be private and fix_hint {env: "GITLAB_TOKEN"}, and exits 1

symbols.name: Client
